Phase 6D Recommendation Campaign Follow-Up Proposal Administrative Ratification
============================================================================

Purpose and recovered roadmap
-----------------------------

Phase 6D records one immutable administrative ratification for one exact eligible
Phase 6C follow-up-proposal review event.  The committed Phase 6A roadmap
separates Phase 6B--6F into persistence, review, ratification/rejection,
activation, and execution concerns.  Phase 6C uses ``approved`` and
``rejected`` as its review outcomes, but explicitly defines an approved review
as evidence for possible consideration by a later separately authorized
phase.  Phase 6D is that distinct administrative ratification boundary; it is not
the later activation or execution boundary.

Only an exact persisted Phase 6C ``approved`` review is eligible.  A rejected,
missing, malformed, stale, identity-inconsistent, or unsupported review cannot
be approved.  Phase 6D never rebuilds the Phase 6A proposal or recomputes the
Phase 5 assessment/policy decision.  It loads the authoritative Phase 6C
record, whose validated repository reload in turn verifies the exact persisted
Phase 6B proposal and complete Phase 6A identity.

Immutable domain contract
-------------------------

``RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalRatification`` is a pure, database-free,
non-assignable contract version 1 value.  It binds:

* the positive generated Phase 6C review-event ID;
* exact Phase 6C review version, canonical text, tagged hash, and approved
  review decision;
* exact reviewed Phase 6B proposal ID and Phase 6A version, canonical text,
  and tagged hash;
* one explicit Phase 6D ``approved`` administrative decision;
* an explicit ratifier identity; and
* a non-empty administrative basis or basis.

Ratifier identity is 1--128 ASCII bytes, begins alphanumerically, and permits
only alphanumerics plus ``._@:/+-``.  Reason text is 1--4096 bytes of valid
UTF-8, preserves its exact bytes, requires a byte other than ASCII space, tab,
carriage return, or line feed, and rejects NUL, DEL, and disallowed control
bytes.

Canonical identity
------------------

The authoritative grammar begins with
``experiment_recommendation_campaign_follow_up_proposal_ratification_v1``.  It
binds the contract version; fixed administrative and negative-authority
semantics; exact review-event, review, and proposal identity; the approved
review and ratification decisions; ratifier; and basis in fixed order.
Delimiter-capable values are byte-length framed.  Integer and length rendering
is locale-independent.  The complete canonical text is limited to 2,113,536
bytes.  Canonical text is authoritative; the tagged FNV-1a hash is only an
accelerator.  Generated ratification-event ID, timestamp, PID, scheduler state, and
future lifecycle state remain outside semantic identity.

Persistence, replay, and concurrency
------------------------------------

Migration ``044`` adds the append-only
``experiment_recommendation_campaign_follow_up_proposal_ratification_event``
table.  Restrictive foreign keys bind both the review event and reviewed
proposal.  An invoker-rights insert trigger, with a pinned schema-qualified
execution context, joins the exact Phase 6C review and Phase 6B proposal and
verifies every copied version/canonical/hash field plus approved eligibility.
One review event and one proposal can each have at most one Phase 6D ratification.

The repository validates the pure value, takes a review-event-ID-scoped
transaction advisory lock, reloads and validates the complete Phase 6C/6B
chain, and inserts only after exact comparison.  The first valid operation
returns ``recorded``.  An exact retry returns ``existing_identical``.  A
different ratifier, basis, identity, or payload for the same review returns
``recommendation_campaign_follow_up_proposal_ratification_conflict`` and never
replaces history.  Concurrent equivalent requests converge on one event;
concurrent conflicting requests yield one winner and one deterministic
conflict.  Hash equality never substitutes for canonical or typed equality.

Repository lookup by ratification-event ID, review-event ID, or proposal ID and
bounded descending list operations are read-only.  They rebuild the immutable
contract, recompute its identity, reload Phase 6C, and validate the complete
upstream binding.  Corrupt or stale persisted evidence fails closed.

Service boundary
----------------

``RatifyRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposal`` requires an explicit Phase
6C review-event ID, expected review identity hash, ratifier, and basis.  In one
transaction it loads the exact review, compares the expected hash, enforces the
approved eligibility decision, builds the pure Phase 6D value, persists it,
and returns the persisted result.  Missing, stale, rejected, malformed, or
conflicting evidence rolls back the transaction.

No main-program CLI or presentation command is added in Phase 6D.  The typed
service is the deliberate application authority for focused verification and
future explicit administrative integration.  This avoids implying that a
newly persisted ratification is an activation or execution command.  Read-only
repository inspection remains available without adding operational routing.

Privileges and immutability
---------------------------

Runtime role ``pqxx`` receives only table ``SELECT``, column-scoped payload
``INSERT``, and sequence ``USAGE``.  It cannot provide the generated event ID
or timestamp and has no table-level insert, update, delete, or truncate
privilege.  ``PUBLIC`` receives no table, sequence, or trigger-function
privilege, including PostgreSQL default-ACL fallback.  The provenance trigger
function is not directly executable by runtime or ``PUBLIC``.

Explicit non-authorities
------------------------

Phase 6D administrative ratification is immutable audit evidence only.  Its domain
canonical fixes ``activated=false``, ``execution_authorized=false``,
``follow_up_authorized=false``, ``queued=false``, ``scheduled=false``,
``scheduler_started=false``, ``scheduler_signaled=false``,
``workers_started=false``, ``experiments_created=false``,
``experiments_modified=false``, and ``campaign_success_declared=false``.

Phase 6D does not activate or execute a campaign, authorize follow-up
execution, queue or schedule work, signal or start the scheduler, launch a
worker, create or modify an experiment/model/recommendation, advance a
continuation, declare success or profitability, perform statistical
validation, auto-review, or auto-ratify.  Negative fields are assertions, not
capabilities.  Later phases continue to own any separately specified
activation and execution authority.

Verification and operational safety
-----------------------------------

Database-free tests cover immutable construction, golden canonical grammar,
deterministic hash, locale independence, exact identity sensitivity,
approved-review eligibility, malformed versions/IDs/hashes, hostile UTF-8 and
control input, operator text, and fixed non-authority.

The repository suite requires an explicitly named clearly disposable database,
rejects case-insensitive ``LSTM``, verifies its connected database before any
migration, and uses per-process schemas.  It covers clean install, upgrade from
pre-existing Phase 6B/6C rows, migration repeatability and ACL fallback,
service eligibility, missing/stale review, exact replay, sequential and
concurrent conflicts, concurrent convergence, rollback, collision/mismatch
failure, append-only privilege denial, restrictive provenance, read-only
lookup/list behavior, and unchanged Phase 6B, Phase 6C, experiment, and
scheduler sentinels.  Test schemas and the disposable database are removed
after verification.

# ADR-0009: Phase 6D separately approves one eligible reviewed follow-up proposal

Status: Accepted
Date: 2026-07-22
Deciders: Project architecture
Affected volumes: Volume VIII §§2–11; Volume XII §§2–11
Supersedes: None
Superseded by: None

## 1. Context and problem statement

Phase 6C records an immutable approved or rejected administrative review for
one exact persisted Phase 6B proposal. Its approved outcome is deliberately
non-authorizing evidence for possible later consideration. The Phase 6A
roadmap also keeps persistence, review, ratification/rejection, activation, and
execution as distinct possible Phase 6B–6F concerns. The next increment needs
one explicit ratification authority without turning reviewed evidence into
activation, execution, scheduling, or experiment capability.

## 2. Decision

Phase 6D defines a pure immutable administrative ratification value, additive
migration 044, an exact-binding append-only repository, and one transactional
service.

- Only an exact persisted Phase 6C `approved` review is eligible. Rejected,
  missing, malformed, stale, or identity-inconsistent reviews fail closed.
- Contract version 1 binds the review-event ID; exact review and proposal
  version/canonical/hash identities; approved review and ratification decisions;
  ratifier; basis; and fixed negative operational semantics.
- Canonical text is authoritative, byte-length framed, locale-independent,
  and bounded. The tagged hash is only an accelerator.
- Migration 044 stores one immutable ratification per review/proposal, retains
  restrictive foreign keys, and verifies the full Phase 6C/6B chain in an
  invoker-rights insert trigger with pinned safe `search_path`.
- A review-event-scoped transaction advisory lock serializes ratification attempts.
  First persistence is `recorded`, exact replay is `existing_identical`, and
  any changed payload for that review conflicts.
- The service loads and validates the exact Phase 6C record, checks an explicit
  expected review hash and eligibility, builds the pure ratification, and persists
  in one transaction.
- Runtime access is SELECT, payload-column INSERT, and sequence USAGE only.
  Existing ratifications cannot be updated, deleted, expired, or superseded.
- No CLI, activation adapter, execution adapter, queue, scheduler call,
  worker launch, or experiment/model/recommendation mutation is added.

Administrative ratification is evidence only. It is explicitly not follow-up or
execution authorization.

## 3. Rationale and decision drivers

- Preserve the roadmap's separate review and ratification authorities despite
  Phase 6C's approved/rejected review terminology.
- Consume authoritative persisted upstream records without recomputing Phase
  5 policy or Phase 6A proposal truth.
- Prevent a stale event ID, hash collision, or copied proposal identity from
  silently approving another review.
- Give retries and concurrent attempts deterministic append-only outcomes.
- Keep every operational capability absent until a later explicit contract.

## 4. Consequences

### 4.1 Positive consequences

- One eligible Phase 6C review can receive at most one immutable Phase 6D
  ratification with explicit human identity and basis.
- Full canonical provenance remains inspectable and typed reload detects
  corruption or upstream disagreement.
- Equivalent concurrent requests converge; conflicting requests cannot replace
  the winner.
- Database privileges and schema constraints preserve append-only least
  privilege independently of application validation.

### 4.2 Negative consequences and trade-offs

- Phase 6C already calls its positive review outcome `approved`, so Phase 6D's
  separate ratification terminology requires careful documentation.
- Full review and proposal canonical values are duplicated for self-contained
  exact provenance and may produce ratification records slightly above two MiB.
- Phase 6D cannot correct a mistaken ratification in place; correction would need
  a separately accepted append-only design.
- No main-program CLI is available in this increment; callers use the typed
  service boundary.

### 4.3 Risks and mitigations

- Authority confusion: fixed negative canonical flags, explicit documentation,
  and absence of all action adapters.
- Hash collision: compare complete canonical text and typed payload after every
  hash match; uniqueness is scoped by review/proposal ID, not hash.
- Upstream drift: two restrictive foreign keys, joined provenance trigger, and
  validated Phase 6C repository reload.
- Race or retry ambiguity: transaction advisory lock plus unique review and
  proposal constraints.
- Privilege escalation: explicit PUBLIC/runtime revokes, column grants,
  invoker rights, pinned function context, and NULL-ACL fallback tests.

## 5. Compatibility and migration

Migration 044 is additive after migration 043. It does not alter Phase 6A,
6B, or 6C records, canonical identities, APIs, or privileges and does not touch
experiment or scheduler tables. It supports both an empty clean installation
and upgrade with existing reviewed proposals. Rollback is not performed by the
implementation; any operational rollback would remove only the new Phase 6D
objects under separately approved administration.

## 6. Verification and operational evidence

- Pure warnings-as-errors tests for immutable semantics, canonical grammar,
  deterministic/locale-independent identity, input validation, eligibility,
  and negative authority.
- Isolated PostgreSQL tests for clean and upgrade migration paths,
  repeatability, exact ACL and NULL-ACL fallback, trigger identity/context,
  provenance, service behavior, replay/conflict, concurrency, rollback,
  collision/mismatch rejection, read-only queries, and upstream sentinels.
- Phase 6A/6B/6C focused regressions, project-file validation, focused source
  integration, and whitespace audit. The incremental Release build is deferred
  while active training workers make added build contention unsafe.
- Tests require a clearly disposable non-`LSTM` database and remove all
  disposable database objects after use.

## 7. Alternatives considered

### 7.1 Treat Phase 6C approved review as Phase 6D ratification

Rejected because the Phase 6A roadmap separates review from ratification and Phase
6C explicitly limits its positive result to possible later consideration.
Collapsing them would erase the next authority boundary rather than implement
it.

### 7.2 Add activation or execution authorization to the ratification record

Rejected because administrative ratification is evidence, while operational
authorization requires a later explicit lifecycle and safety design.

### 7.3 Rebuild the proposal or policy decision in the service

Rejected because Phase 6B and Phase 6C are authoritative persisted records.
Recomputation could drift and reopen accepted scientific or review decisions.

### 7.4 Add a main-program CLI now

Rejected for this increment because the typed service fully establishes and
tests the authority, while a CLI could imply operational follow-up semantics
before a later activation/execution contract exists.

# Architecture Decision Records

## 1. Purpose

Architecture Decision Records preserve the context, decision, alternatives,
and consequences of material architectural choices. ADRs explain why the
architecture has its current shape; domain volumes describe the resulting
ongoing contract.

## 2. Numbering and filenames

- Numbers are four digits, monotonic, and never reused: `ADR-0001`.
- Filename format is `ADR-NNNN-short-kebab-title.md`.
- A reserved or rejected number remains consumed.
- Renaming the title does not change the number.
- The next ADR number is one greater than the highest number present here.

## 3. Status values

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Proposed` | Under review; not implementation authority. |
| `Accepted` | Approved and governing from its decision date. |
| `Rejected` | Considered and declined; retained as rationale. |
| `Deprecated` | Still historical, but no longer recommended for new work. |
| `Superseded by ADR-NNNN` | Replaced by a later accepted decision. |

Accepted ADRs are immutable decision records. Editorial corrections may fix
links or spelling without changing meaning and must be noted in revision
history. A changed decision receives a new ADR that supersedes the old one.

## 4. Changes requiring an ADR

Volume I §16.1 is authoritative. Typical triggers include identity semantics,
durable ownership, schema strategy, transaction/concurrency rules, scheduler
scope, lifecycle transitions, recommendation conversion, security/privileges,
and breaking public-interface changes.

## 5. Required sections

Every ADR MUST contain:

1. Title and metadata: number, status, date, deciders, affected volumes.
2. Context and problem statement.
3. Decision.
4. Rationale and decision drivers.
5. Consequences, both positive and negative.
6. Compatibility and migration.
7. Verification and operational evidence.
8. Alternatives considered.
9. References.
10. Revision history.

The [ADR template](ADR_TEMPLATE.md) is normative for new records.

## 6. Proposal workflow

1. Copy `ADR_TEMPLATE.md` to the next numbered filename.
2. Set status `Proposed` and identify affected volume sections.
3. Describe the problem independently from the preferred solution.
4. Record alternatives, compatibility, migration, rollback, concurrency,
   permissions, operational safety, and tests.
5. Review against Volume I and all affected accepted ADRs.
6. Record the decision status without deleting rejected alternatives.
7. Update affected volumes and their revision histories when accepted.
8. Implement only after acceptance unless Volume I §16.4 applies.

## 7. Index

| ADR | Status | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| [ADR-0001](ADR-0001-postgresql-source-of-truth.md) | Accepted | PostgreSQL is the durable source of truth. |
| [ADR-0002](ADR-0002-deterministic-experiment-identity.md) | Accepted | Experiment semantic identity uses deterministic canonical content. |
| [ADR-0003](ADR-0003-advisory-recommendation-evaluation.md) | Accepted | Recommendation generation, scoring, and review remain advisory and non-executing. |
| [ADR-0004](ADR-0004-scheduler-ownership-boundaries.md) | Accepted | Scheduler work requires explicit ownership and durable lifecycle claims. |
| [ADR-0005](ADR-0005-manual-recommendation-conversion.md) | Accepted | Explicit approved-proposal conversion creates one paused experiment. |
| [ADR-0006](ADR-0006-phase-6a-follow-up-proposal.md) | Accepted | Phase 6A follow-up proposals are pure, identity-bound, and non-authorizing. |
| [ADR-0007](ADR-0007-phase-6b-follow-up-proposal-persistence.md) | Accepted | Phase 6B persists exact advisory proposals for read-only preview without action authority. |
| [ADR-0008](ADR-0008-phase-6c-follow-up-proposal-administrative-review.md) | Accepted | Phase 6C records one immutable administrative proposal review without action authority. |
| [ADR-0009](ADR-0009-phase-6d-follow-up-proposal-governance-ratification.md) | Accepted | Phase 6D separately approves one exact eligible reviewed follow-up proposal without action authority. |

-Phase 6D Recommendation Campaign Follow-Up Proposal Administrative Ratification
-============================================================================
+Phase 6D Recommendation Campaign Follow-Up Proposal Governance Ratification
+===========================================================================
 
-Purpose and recovered roadmap
------------------------------
+Purpose and distinct authority
+------------------------------
 
-Phase 6D records one immutable administrative ratification for one exact eligible
-Phase 6C follow-up-proposal review event.  The committed Phase 6A roadmap
-separates Phase 6B--6F into persistence, review, ratification/rejection,
-activation, and execution concerns.  Phase 6C uses ``approved`` and
-``rejected`` as its review outcomes, but explicitly defines an approved review
-as evidence for possible consideration by a later separately authorized
-phase.  Phase 6D is that distinct administrative ratification boundary; it is not
-the later activation or execution boundary.
+Phase 6C and Phase 6D answer different governance questions.
 
-Only an exact persisted Phase 6C ``approved`` review is eligible.  A rejected,
-missing, malformed, stale, identity-inconsistent, or unsupported review cannot
-be approved.  Phase 6D never rebuilds the Phase 6A proposal or recomputes the
-Phase 5 assessment/policy decision.  It loads the authoritative Phase 6C
-record, whose validated repository reload in turn verifies the exact persisted
-Phase 6B proposal and complete Phase 6A identity.
+Phase 6C asks whether one exact persisted Phase 6B follow-up proposal is
+acceptable on its merits for possible advancement.  An identified reviewer
+records one immutable ``approved`` or ``rejected`` administrative review.
 
+Phase 6D asks whether, given that exact approved review and its complete
+authoritative provenance, an authorized governance actor ratifies advancement
+of the reviewed proposal into the next separately controlled phase.  The only
+positive Phase 6D decision is ``ratified``.  Ratification is immutable
+governance evidence; it does not grant any capability in Phase 6E.
+
+Eligibility and separation of duties
+------------------------------------
+
+Only one exact persisted, fully reloadable Phase 6C ``approved`` review is
+eligible.  A rejected, missing, malformed, stale, unsupported, or
+identity-inconsistent review fails closed.  The ratifier identity must differ
+byte-for-byte from the Phase 6C reviewer identity.  Self-ratification is
+rejected by pure construction, service and repository validation, a database
+check constraint, and the provenance trigger.
+
+The ratifier acts under the fixed version-1 role
+``follow_up_governance_ratifier``.  Callers cannot select or inject a different

+no experiment, model, continuation, lifecycle, queue, or scheduler table.

+Eligibility and separation of duties
+------------------------------------
+
+Only one exact persisted, fully reloadable Phase 6C ``approved`` review is
+eligible.  A rejected, missing, malformed, stale, unsupported, or
+identity-inconsistent review fails closed.  The ratifier identity must differ
+byte-for-byte from the Phase 6C reviewer identity.  Self-ratification is
+rejected by pure construction, service and repository validation, a database
+check constraint, and the provenance trigger.
+
+The ratifier acts under the fixed version-1 role
+``follow_up_governance_ratifier``.  Callers cannot select or inject a different
+role.  Phase 6D never rebuilds the Phase 6A proposal or recomputes Phase 5
+assessment or policy truth; validated Phase 6C reload transitively validates
+the exact persisted Phase 6B proposal and embedded Phase 6A identity.

+records one immutable ``approved`` or ``rejected`` administrative review.
 
+Phase 6D asks whether, given that exact approved review and its complete
+authoritative provenance, an authorized governance actor ratifies advancement
+of the reviewed proposal into the next separately controlled phase.  The only
+positive Phase 6D decision is ``ratified``.  Ratification is immutable
+governance evidence; it does not grant any capability in Phase 6E.
+
+Eligibility and separation of duties
+------------------------------------
+
+Only one exact persisted, fully reloadable Phase 6C ``approved`` review is
+eligible.  A rejected, missing, malformed, stale, unsupported, or
+identity-inconsistent review fails closed.  The ratifier identity must differ
+byte-for-byte from the Phase 6C reviewer identity.  Self-ratification is
+rejected by pure construction, service and repository validation, a database
+check constraint, and the provenance trigger.
+
+The ratifier acts under the fixed version-1 role
+``follow_up_governance_ratifier``.  Callers cannot select or inject a different
+role.  Phase 6D never rebuilds the Phase 6A proposal or recomputes Phase 5
+assessment or policy truth; validated Phase 6C reload transitively validates
+the exact persisted Phase 6B proposal and embedded Phase 6A identity.
+

+------------------------------------
+
+Only one exact persisted, fully reloadable Phase 6C ``approved`` review is

+role.  Phase 6D never rebuilds the Phase 6A proposal or recomputes Phase 5

+Eligibility and separation of duties
+------------------------------------
+
+Only one exact persisted, fully reloadable Phase 6C ``approved`` review is
+eligible.  A rejected, missing, malformed, stale, unsupported, or
+identity-inconsistent review fails closed.  The ratifier identity must differ
+byte-for-byte from the Phase 6C reviewer identity.  Self-ratification is
+rejected by pure construction, service and repository validation, a database
+check constraint, and the provenance trigger.
+
+The ratifier acts under the fixed version-1 role
+``follow_up_governance_ratifier``.  Callers cannot select or inject a different
+role.  Phase 6D never rebuilds the Phase 6A proposal or recomputes Phase 5
+assessment or policy truth; validated Phase 6C reload transitively validates
+the exact persisted Phase 6B proposal and embedded Phase 6A identity.

+Phase 6D Recommendation Campaign Follow-Up Proposal Governance Ratification

-Purpose and recovered roadmap

+Purpose and distinct authority
+------------------------------
 
-Phase 6D records one immutable administrative ratification for one exact eligible
-Phase 6C follow-up-proposal review event.  The committed Phase 6A roadmap
-separates Phase 6B--6F into persistence, review, ratification/rejection,
-activation, and execution concerns.  Phase 6C uses ``approved`` and

+Phase 6C and Phase 6D answer different governance questions.
 
-Only an exact persisted Phase 6C ``approved`` review is eligible.  A rejected,
-missing, malformed, stale, identity-inconsistent, or unsupported review cannot
-be approved.  Phase 6D never rebuilds the Phase 6A proposal or recomputes the

-record, whose validated repository reload in turn verifies the exact persisted
-Phase 6B proposal and complete Phase 6A identity.
+Phase 6C asks whether one exact persisted Phase 6B follow-up proposal is
+acceptable on its merits for possible advancement.  An identified reviewer
+records one immutable ``approved`` or ``rejected`` administrative review.
 
+Phase 6D asks whether, given that exact approved review and its complete
+authoritative provenance, an authorized governance actor ratifies advancement
+of the reviewed proposal into the next separately controlled phase.  The only
+positive Phase 6D decision is ``ratified``.  Ratification is immutable
+governance evidence; it does not grant any capability in Phase 6E.
+
+Eligibility and separation of duties
+------------------------------------
+
+Only one exact persisted, fully reloadable Phase 6C ``approved`` review is
+eligible.  A rejected, missing, malformed, stale, unsupported, or
+identity-inconsistent review fails closed.  The ratifier identity must differ
+byte-for-byte from the Phase 6C reviewer identity.  Self-ratification is
+rejected by pure construction, service and repository validation, a database
+check constraint, and the provenance trigger.
+
+The ratifier acts under the fixed version-1 role
+``follow_up_governance_ratifier``.  Callers cannot select or inject a different
+role.  Phase 6D never rebuilds the Phase 6A proposal or recomputes Phase 5
+assessment or policy truth; validated Phase 6C reload transitively validates
+the exact persisted Phase 6B proposal and embedded Phase 6A identity.
+

+Eligibility and separation of duties
+------------------------------------
+
+Only one exact persisted, fully reloadable Phase 6C ``approved`` review is
+eligible.  A rejected, missing, malformed, stale, unsupported, or
+identity-inconsistent review fails closed.  The ratifier identity must differ
+byte-for-byte from the Phase 6C reviewer identity.  Self-ratification is
+rejected by pure construction, service and repository validation, a database
+check constraint, and the provenance trigger.
+
+The ratifier acts under the fixed version-1 role
+``follow_up_governance_ratifier``.  Callers cannot select or inject a different
+role.  Phase 6D never rebuilds the Phase 6A proposal or recomputes Phase 5
+assessment or policy truth; validated Phase 6C reload transitively validates
+the exact persisted Phase 6B proposal and embedded Phase 6A identity.

+Phase 6D Recommendation Campaign Follow-Up Proposal Governance Ratification

+Purpose and distinct authority
+------------------------------
 
-Phase 6D records one immutable administrative ratification for one exact eligible
-Phase 6C follow-up-proposal review event.  The committed Phase 6A roadmap
-separates Phase 6B--6F into persistence, review, ratification/rejection,
-activation, and execution concerns.  Phase 6C uses ``approved`` and

-Only an exact persisted Phase 6C ``approved`` review is eligible.  A rejected,
-missing, malformed, stale, identity-inconsistent, or unsupported review cannot
-be approved.  Phase 6D never rebuilds the Phase 6A proposal or recomputes the

+Phase 6C asks whether one exact persisted Phase 6B follow-up proposal is
+acceptable on its merits for possible advancement.  An identified reviewer
+records one immutable ``approved`` or ``rejected`` administrative review.
 
+Phase 6D asks whether, given that exact approved review and its complete
+authoritative provenance, an authorized governance actor ratifies advancement
+of the reviewed proposal into the next separately controlled phase.  The only
+positive Phase 6D decision is ``ratified``.  Ratification is immutable
+governance evidence; it does not grant any capability in Phase 6E.

+Eligibility and separation of duties
+------------------------------------
+
+Only one exact persisted, fully reloadable Phase 6C ``approved`` review is
+eligible.  A rejected, missing, malformed, stale, unsupported, or
+identity-inconsistent review fails closed.  The ratifier identity must differ
+byte-for-byte from the Phase 6C reviewer identity.  Self-ratification is
+rejected by pure construction, service and repository validation, a database
+check constraint, and the provenance trigger.
+
+The ratifier acts under the fixed version-1 role
+``follow_up_governance_ratifier``.  Callers cannot select or inject a different
+role.  Phase 6D never rebuilds the Phase 6A proposal or recomputes Phase 5
+assessment or policy truth; validated Phase 6C reload transitively validates
+the exact persisted Phase 6B proposal and embedded Phase 6A identity.
+

+Phase 6D Recommendation Campaign Follow-Up Proposal Governance Ratification
+===========================================================================
 
-Purpose and recovered roadmap
------------------------------
+Purpose and distinct authority
+------------------------------
 
-Phase 6D records one immutable administrative ratification for one exact eligible
-Phase 6C follow-up-proposal review event.  The committed Phase 6A roadmap
-separates Phase 6B--6F into persistence, review, ratification/rejection,
-activation, and execution concerns.  Phase 6C uses ``approved`` and
-``rejected`` as its review outcomes, but explicitly defines an approved review
-as evidence for possible consideration by a later separately authorized
-phase.  Phase 6D is that distinct administrative ratification boundary; it is not

+Phase 6C and Phase 6D answer different governance questions.
 
-Only an exact persisted Phase 6C ``approved`` review is eligible.  A rejected,
-missing, malformed, stale, identity-inconsistent, or unsupported review cannot
-be approved.  Phase 6D never rebuilds the Phase 6A proposal or recomputes the
-Phase 5 assessment/policy decision.  It loads the authoritative Phase 6C
-record, whose validated repository reload in turn verifies the exact persisted
-Phase 6B proposal and complete Phase 6A identity.
+Phase 6C asks whether one exact persisted Phase 6B follow-up proposal is
+acceptable on its merits for possible advancement.  An identified reviewer
+records one immutable ``approved`` or ``rejected`` administrative review.
 
+Phase 6D asks whether, given that exact approved review and its complete
+authoritative provenance, an authorized governance actor ratifies advancement
+of the reviewed proposal into the next separately controlled phase.  The only
+positive Phase 6D decision is ``ratified``.  Ratification is immutable
+governance evidence; it does not grant any capability in Phase 6E.
+
+Eligibility and separation of duties
+------------------------------------
+
+Only one exact persisted, fully reloadable Phase 6C ``approved`` review is
+eligible.  A rejected, missing, malformed, stale, unsupported, or
+identity-inconsistent review fails closed.  The ratifier identity must differ

The second run found another PostgreSQL 63-byte identifier edge introduced by the longer word “ratification”: the generated event-ID column was silently truncated, so `pg_get_serial_sequence` could not resolve its textual name. I’m correcting the new Phase 6D object names to explicit ratification identifiers that fit PostgreSQL’s limit, including the table, ID column, index, trigger, and function, instead of relying on silent truncation. No upstream schema is changing.

+------------------------------------
+
+Only one exact persisted, fully reloadable Phase 6C ``approved`` review is

+role.  Phase 6D never rebuilds the Phase 6A proposal or recomputes Phase 5

+Phase 6C `approved` review is eligible, the fixed role is
+`follow_up_governance_ratifier`, and the ratifier must differ from the Phase 6C
+reviewer. Restrictive review/proposal foreign keys, checks, and an
+invoker-rights provenance trigger verify the complete copied
+version/canonical/hash chain and separation of duties. Exact replay is
+idempotent; any changed ratifier, basis, role, or identity conflicts.
 Runtime access is limited to `SELECT`, column-scoped `INSERT`, and sequence
 `USAGE`, with explicit PUBLIC and trigger-function revocation. Phase 6D
-approval remains non-operational evidence: it does not authorize follow-up or
-execution, activate, queue, schedule, signal/start the scheduler, launch a
-worker, create/modify an experiment or model, or declare campaign success.
+ratification remains non-operational evidence: it grants no Phase 6E
+capability and does not authorize follow-up or execution, activate, queue,
+schedule, signal/start the scheduler, launch a worker, create/modify an
+experiment or model, or declare campaign success.
 
 The scheduler and analyzer expect these migrations to be applied before running
 `--schedule-experiments`, `--enqueue-experiment`, or leaderboard commands.

+Eligibility and separation of duties
+------------------------------------
+
+Only one exact persisted, fully reloadable Phase 6C ``approved`` review is
+eligible.  A rejected, missing, malformed, stale, unsupported, or
+identity-inconsistent review fails closed.  The ratifier identity must differ
+byte-for-byte from the Phase 6C reviewer identity.  Self-ratification is
+rejected by pure construction, service and repository validation, a database
+check constraint, and the provenance trigger.
+
+The ratifier acts under the fixed version-1 role
+``follow_up_governance_ratifier``.  Callers cannot select or inject a different
+role.  Phase 6D never rebuilds the Phase 6A proposal or recomputes Phase 5
+assessment or policy truth; validated Phase 6C reload transitively validates
+the exact persisted Phase 6B proposal and embedded Phase 6A identity.

 ## 3. Rationale and decision drivers
 
-- Preserve the roadmap's separate review and ratification authorities despite
-  Phase 6C's approved/rejected review terminology.
-- Consume authoritative persisted upstream records without recomputing Phase
-  5 policy or Phase 6A proposal truth.
-- Prevent a stale event ID, hash collision, or copied proposal identity from
-  silently approving another review.
-- Give retries and concurrent attempts deterministic append-only outcomes.
-- Keep every operational capability absent until a later explicit contract.
+- Give Phase 6D a materially distinct governance question and consequence.
+- Require independent human accountability at the advancement boundary.
+- Consume authoritative persisted evidence without recomputing Phase 5 or
+  Phase 6A truth.
+- Preserve canonical-first collision safety and deterministic retry behavior.
+- Keep every operational capability absent until separately designed and
+  accepted.
 
 ## 4. Consequences
 
 ### 4.1 Positive consequences
 
-- One eligible Phase 6C review can receive at most one immutable Phase 6D
-  ratification with explicit human identity and basis.
-- Full canonical provenance remains inspectable and typed reload detects
-  corruption or upstream disagreement.
-- Equivalent concurrent requests converge; conflicting requests cannot replace
-  the winner.
-- Database privileges and schema constraints preserve append-only least
-  privilege independently of application validation.
+- The audit trail distinguishes proposal merits review from governance
+  ratification of advancement.
+- One actor cannot both approve the Phase 6C review and ratify it in Phase 6D.
+- Full typed provenance and defense-in-depth database enforcement detect stale,
+  forged, malformed, or self-ratified evidence.
+- Equivalent retries and concurrent requests converge without replacing
+  history.
 
 ### 4.2 Negative consequences and trade-offs

-  separate ratification terminology requires careful documentation.
-- Full review and proposal canonical values are duplicated for self-contained
-  exact provenance and may produce ratification records slightly above two MiB.
-- Phase 6D cannot correct a mistaken ratification in place; correction would need
+- A second governance actor is required before a proposal can be ratified.
+- Complete review and proposal canonical text is duplicated and may exceed two
+  MiB per event.
+- A mistaken ratification cannot be changed in place; correction would require
   a separately accepted append-only design.
-- No main-program CLI is available in this increment; callers use the typed
-  service boundary.
+- No main-program CLI exists in this increment.

-  and absence of all action adapters.

-  hash match; uniqueness is scoped by review/proposal ID, not hash.
-- Upstream drift: two restrictive foreign keys, joined provenance trigger, and
+- Semantic duplication: distinct question, `ratified` decision, fixed role,

  expertadvisor_phase6d_ratification_test_*) ;;
  *) echo disposable_database_name_rejected >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

  echo refusing_existing_database="$phase6d_test_db" >&2
  exit 2
fi

template <typename Function>
void AssertRuntimeError(Function&& function, const std::string& expected)
{
    bool rejected = false;
    std::string actualMessage;
    try
    {
        function();
    }
    catch (const std::runtime_error& error)
    {
        rejected = error.what() == expected;
    }
    assert(rejected);
}

template <typename Function>
void AssertInvalidArgument(Function&& function, const std::string& expected)
{
    bool rejected = false;
    try
    {
        function();
    }
    catch (const std::invalid_argument& error)
    {
        rejected = error.what() == expected;
    }
    assert(rejected);
}

template <typename Corruption>
void AssertMalformedReloadRejected(
    pqxx::connection& owner,
    const std::string& schema,
    long long ratificationEventId,
    Corruption&& corruption,
    const std::string& expectedFragment)
{
    bool rejected = false;
    {
        pqxx::work transaction{owner};
        SetSearchPath(transaction, schema);
        corruption(transaction);
        try
        {
            (void)FindRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalRatification(
                transaction, ratificationEventId);
        }
        catch (const std::runtime_error& error)
        {
            actualMessage = error.what();
            rejected = actualMessage.starts_with(
                           "invalid_persisted_recommendation_campaign_"
                           "follow_up_proposal_ratification:") &&
                actualMessage.find(expectedFragment) != std::string::npos;
        }
    }
    if (!rejected)
        std::cerr << "malformed_reload_expected=" << expectedFragment
                  << " actual=" << actualMessage << '\n';
    assert(rejected);
}

template <typename Function>
void AssertRuntimeError(Function&& function, const std::string& expected)
{
    bool rejected = false;
    try
    {
        function();
    }
    catch (const std::runtime_error& error)
    {
        rejected = error.what() == expected;
    }
    assert(rejected);
}

template <typename Function>
void AssertInvalidArgument(Function&& function, const std::string& expected)
{
    bool rejected = false;
    try
    {
        function();
    }
    catch (const std::invalid_argument& error)
    {
        rejected = error.what() == expected;
    }
    assert(rejected);
}

+Eligibility and separation of duties
+------------------------------------
+
+Only one exact persisted, fully reloadable Phase 6C ``approved`` review is

+role.  Phase 6D never rebuilds the Phase 6A proposal or recomputes Phase 5

+------------------------------------

+role.  Phase 6D never rebuilds the Phase 6A proposal or recomputes Phase 5

-  Phase 6C's approved/rejected review terminology.

-  silently approving another review.

 ## 4. Consequences

-- One eligible Phase 6C review can receive at most one immutable Phase 6D
-  ratification with explicit human identity and basis.

-  corruption or upstream disagreement.
-- Equivalent concurrent requests converge; conflicting requests cannot replace
-  the winner.
-- Database privileges and schema constraints preserve append-only least
-  privilege independently of application validation.
+- The audit trail distinguishes proposal merits review from governance
+  ratification of advancement.
+- One actor cannot both approve the Phase 6C review and ratify it in Phase 6D.

+  forged, malformed, or self-ratified evidence.
+- Equivalent retries and concurrent requests converge without replacing
+  history.

 ## 7. Alternatives considered
 
-### 7.1 Treat Phase 6C approved review as Phase 6D ratification
+### 7.1 Keep a second administrative approval
 
-Rejected because the Phase 6A roadmap separates review from ratification and Phase
-6C explicitly limits its positive result to possible later consideration.

+Rejected because it repeats Phase 6C without a distinct question, role,
+policy, or consequence.

+### 7.2 Allow the Phase 6C reviewer to ratify
 
-Rejected because administrative ratification is evidence, while operational
-authorization requires a later explicit lifecycle and safety design.
+Rejected because no committed authority permits self-ratification and it
+would remove the independent governance check that distinguishes Phase 6D.
 
-### 7.3 Rebuild the proposal or policy decision in the service
+### 7.3 Treat Phase 6C approval as automatic ratification

-  Phase 6C's approved/rejected review terminology.

-  the winner.

-  privilege independently of application validation.

+  ratification of advancement.

-  Phase 6C's approved/rejected review terminology.
-- Consume authoritative persisted upstream records without recomputing Phase
-  5 policy or Phase 6A proposal truth.
-- Prevent a stale event ID, hash collision, or copied proposal identity from
-  silently approving another review.
-- Give retries and concurrent attempts deterministic append-only outcomes.
-- Keep every operational capability absent until a later explicit contract.
+- Give Phase 6D a materially distinct governance question and consequence.
+- Require independent human accountability at the advancement boundary.
+- Consume authoritative persisted evidence without recomputing Phase 5 or
+  Phase 6A truth.
+- Preserve canonical-first collision safety and deterministic retry behavior.
+- Keep every operational capability absent until separately designed and
+  accepted.
 
 ## 4. Consequences
 
 ### 4.1 Positive consequences
 
-- One eligible Phase 6C review can receive at most one immutable Phase 6D
-  ratification with explicit human identity and basis.
-- Full canonical provenance remains inspectable and typed reload detects
-  corruption or upstream disagreement.
-- Equivalent concurrent requests converge; conflicting requests cannot replace
-  the winner.
-- Database privileges and schema constraints preserve append-only least
-  privilege independently of application validation.
+- The audit trail distinguishes proposal merits review from governance
+  ratification of advancement.
+- One actor cannot both approve the Phase 6C review and ratify it in Phase 6D.
+- Full typed provenance and defense-in-depth database enforcement detect stale,
+  forged, malformed, or self-ratified evidence.
+- Equivalent retries and concurrent requests converge without replacing
+  history.
 
 ### 4.2 Negative consequences and trade-offs
 
-- Phase 6C already calls its positive review outcome `approved`, so Phase 6D's
-  separate ratification terminology requires careful documentation.
-- Full review and proposal canonical values are duplicated for self-contained
-  exact provenance and may produce ratification records slightly above two MiB.
-- Phase 6D cannot correct a mistaken ratification in place; correction would need
+- A second governance actor is required before a proposal can be ratified.
+- Complete review and proposal canonical text is duplicated and may exceed two
+  MiB per event.
+- A mistaken ratification cannot be changed in place; correction would require
   a separately accepted append-only design.
-- No main-program CLI is available in this increment; callers use the typed
-  service boundary.
+- No main-program CLI exists in this increment.
 
 ### 4.3 Risks and mitigations
 
-- Authority confusion: fixed negative canonical flags, explicit documentation,
-  and absence of all action adapters.
-- Hash collision: compare complete canonical text and typed payload after every
-  hash match; uniqueness is scoped by review/proposal ID, not hash.
-- Upstream drift: two restrictive foreign keys, joined provenance trigger, and
+- Semantic duplication: distinct question, `ratified` decision, fixed role,
+  separation policy, and advancement-only canonical semantics.
+- Self-ratification: pure, service, repository, check-constraint, and trigger
+  enforcement.
+- Hash collision: compare complete authoritative canonical and typed payload.
+- Upstream drift: restrictive foreign keys, joined provenance trigger, and
   validated Phase 6C repository reload.
-- Race or retry ambiguity: transaction advisory lock plus unique review and
-  proposal constraints.
 - Privilege escalation: explicit PUBLIC/runtime revokes, column grants,
-  invoker rights, pinned function context, and NULL-ACL fallback tests.
+  invoker rights, pinned search path, and NULL-ACL fallback tests.
 
 ## 5. Compatibility and migration
 
-Migration 044 is additive after migration 043. It does not alter Phase 6A,
-6B, or 6C records, canonical identities, APIs, or privileges and does not touch
-experiment or scheduler tables. It supports both an empty clean installation
-and upgrade with existing reviewed proposals. Rollback is not performed by the
-implementation; any operational rollback would remove only the new Phase 6D
-objects under separately approved administration.
+Migration 044 is uncommitted and undeployed, so it is replaced in place rather
+than followed by migration 045. It is additive after migration 043 and does
+not alter Phase 6A, 6B, or 6C rows, identities, APIs, or privileges. It touches
+no experiment, model, continuation, lifecycle, queue, or scheduler table.

-Phase 6D Recommendation Campaign Follow-Up Proposal Administrative Ratification
-============================================================================
+Phase 6D Recommendation Campaign Follow-Up Proposal Governance Ratification
+===========================================================================
 
-Purpose and recovered roadmap
------------------------------
+Purpose and distinct authority
+------------------------------
 
-Phase 6D records one immutable administrative ratification for one exact eligible
-Phase 6C follow-up-proposal review event.  The committed Phase 6A roadmap
-separates Phase 6B--6F into persistence, review, ratification/rejection,
-activation, and execution concerns.  Phase 6C uses ``approved`` and
-``rejected`` as its review outcomes, but explicitly defines an approved review
-as evidence for possible consideration by a later separately authorized
-phase.  Phase 6D is that distinct administrative ratification boundary; it is not
-the later activation or execution boundary.
+Phase 6C and Phase 6D answer different governance questions.
 
-Only an exact persisted Phase 6C ``approved`` review is eligible.  A rejected,
-missing, malformed, stale, identity-inconsistent, or unsupported review cannot
-be approved.  Phase 6D never rebuilds the Phase 6A proposal or recomputes the
-Phase 5 assessment/policy decision.  It loads the authoritative Phase 6C
-record, whose validated repository reload in turn verifies the exact persisted
-Phase 6B proposal and complete Phase 6A identity.
+Phase 6C asks whether one exact persisted Phase 6B follow-up proposal is
+acceptable on its merits for possible advancement.  An identified reviewer
+records one immutable ``approved`` or ``rejected`` administrative review.
 
+Phase 6D asks whether, given that exact approved review and its complete
+authoritative provenance, an authorized governance actor ratifies advancement
+of the reviewed proposal into the next separately controlled phase.  The only
+positive Phase 6D decision is ``ratified``.  Ratification is immutable
+governance evidence; it does not grant any capability in Phase 6E.
+
+Eligibility and separation of duties
+------------------------------------
+
+Only one exact persisted, fully reloadable Phase 6C ``approved`` review is
+eligible.  A rejected, missing, malformed, stale, unsupported, or
+identity-inconsistent review fails closed.  The ratifier identity must differ
+byte-for-byte from the Phase 6C reviewer identity.  Self-ratification is
+rejected by pure construction, service and repository validation, a database
+check constraint, and the provenance trigger.
+
+The ratifier acts under the fixed version-1 role
+``follow_up_governance_ratifier``.  Callers cannot select or inject a different
+role.  Phase 6D never rebuilds the Phase 6A proposal or recomputes Phase 5
+assessment or policy truth; validated Phase 6C reload transitively validates
+the exact persisted Phase 6B proposal and embedded Phase 6A identity.
+
 Immutable domain contract
 -------------------------

 ## 4. Consequences

#include "ExperimentRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalRatification.hpp"

bool IsAsciiAlphanumeric(unsigned char character)
{
    return (character >= 'a' && character <= 'z') ||
        (character >= 'A' && character <= 'Z') ||
        (character >= '0' && character <= '9');
}

bool IsValidGovernanceActorIdentity(const std::string& value)
{
    if (value.empty() ||
        value.size() >
            kMaximumRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalRatifierIdentityBytes ||
        !IsAsciiAlphanumeric(static_cast<unsigned char>(value.front())))
        return false;
    for (const unsigned char character : value)
    {
        if (!IsAsciiAlphanumeric(character) && character != '.' &&
            character != '_' && character != '@' && character != ':' &&
            character != '/' && character != '+' && character != '-')
            return false;
    }
    return true;
}

bool IsValidUtf8(const std::string& value)
{
    const auto* bytes = reinterpret_cast<const unsigned char*>(value.data());
    std::size_t index = 0;
    while (index < value.size())
    {
        const unsigned char first = bytes[index];
        if (first <= 0x7fU)
        {
            ++index;
            continue;
        }
        std::size_t continuationCount = 0;
        unsigned int codePoint = 0;
        if (first >= 0xc2U && first <= 0xdfU)
        {
            continuationCount = 1;
            codePoint = first & 0x1fU;
        }
        else if (first >= 0xe0U && first <= 0xefU)
        {
            continuationCount = 2;
            codePoint = first & 0x0fU;
        }
        else if (first >= 0xf0U && first <= 0xf4U)
        {
            continuationCount = 3;
            codePoint = first & 0x07U;
        }
        else return false;
        if (index + continuationCount >= value.size()) return false;
        for (std::size_t offset = 1; offset <= continuationCount; ++offset)
        {
            const unsigned char next = bytes[index + offset];
            if ((next & 0xc0U) != 0x80U) return false;
            codePoint = (codePoint << 6U) | (next & 0x3fU);
        }
        if ((continuationCount == 2 && codePoint < 0x800U) ||
            (continuationCount == 3 && codePoint < 0x10000U) ||
            (codePoint >= 0xd800U && codePoint <= 0xdfffU) ||
            codePoint > 0x10ffffU)
            return false;
        index += continuationCount + 1;
    }
    return true;
}

bool IsValidBasis(const std::string& value)
{
    if (value.empty() ||
        value.size() >
            kMaximumRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalRatificationBasisBytes ||
        !IsValidUtf8(value))
        return false;
    bool containsNonWhitespace = false;
    for (const unsigned char character : value)
    {
        if (character == 0U || character == 0x7fU ||
            (character < 0x20U && character != '\t' && character != '\n' &&
                character != '\r'))
            return false;
        if (character >= 0x80U ||
            (character != ' ' && character != '\t' && character != '\n' &&
                character != '\r'))
            containsNonWhitespace = true;
    }
    return containsNonWhitespace;
}

std::string LengthPrefixed(const std::string& value)
{
    return std::to_string(value.size()) + ":" + value;
}

            throw std::invalid_argument("persisted_proposal_id_invalid");

            proposalCanonicalText.size() >
                kMaximumRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalCanonicalTextBytes ||

                proposalCanonicalText))

            decision);

            kRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalRatificationAuthorityRole)

            ratifierIdentity);

            throw std::invalid_argument(

        ValidateRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalRatificationBasis(
            ratificationBasis);

            reviewContractVersion, reviewCanonicalText, reviewIdentityHash,

            throw std::invalid_argument("ratification_canonical_size_exceeded");

            ratificationContractVersion, canonicalText,
            RecommendationCanonicalHash(canonicalText));

+bool ReviewIdentityMatchesPayload(
+    int reviewContractVersion,
+    const std::string& reviewCanonicalText,
+    const std::string& reviewIdentityHash,
+    long long followUpProposalId,
+    int proposalContractVersion,
+    const std::string& proposalCanonicalText,
+    const std::string& proposalIdentityHash,
+    RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalReviewDecision reviewDecision,
+    const std::string& reviewerIdentity)
+{
+    const std::string marker =
+        ";reviewer=" + LengthPrefixed(reviewerIdentity) + ";reason=";
+    std::size_t markerPosition = reviewCanonicalText.find(marker);
+    while (markerPosition != std::string::npos)
+    {
+        const std::size_t lengthPosition = markerPosition + marker.size();
+        const std::size_t colonPosition =
+            reviewCanonicalText.find(':', lengthPosition);
+        if (colonPosition != std::string::npos &&
+            colonPosition > lengthPosition)
+        {
+            std::size_t reasonLength = 0U;
+            bool validLength = true;
+            for (std::size_t index = lengthPosition;
+                 index < colonPosition; ++index)
+            {
+                const unsigned char character =
+                    static_cast<unsigned char>(reviewCanonicalText[index]);
+                if (character < '0' || character > '9')
+                {
+                    validLength = false;
+                    break;
+                }
+                const std::size_t digit = character - '0';
+                if (reasonLength >
+                    (std::numeric_limits<std::size_t>::max() - digit) / 10U)
+                {
+                    validLength = false;
+                    break;
+                }
+                reasonLength = reasonLength * 10U + digit;
+            }
+            const std::size_t reasonPosition = colonPosition + 1U;
+            if (validLength && reasonLength ==
+                    reviewCanonicalText.size() - reasonPosition)
+            {
+                try
+                {
+                    const auto review =
+                        BuildRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalReview(
+                            reviewContractVersion, followUpProposalId,
+                            proposalContractVersion, proposalCanonicalText,
+                            proposalIdentityHash, reviewDecision,
+                            reviewerIdentity,
+                            reviewCanonicalText.substr(reasonPosition));
+                    if (review.identity.canonicalText == reviewCanonicalText &&
+                        review.identity.hash == reviewIdentityHash)
+                        return true;
+                }
+                catch (const std::exception&)
+                {
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        markerPosition = reviewCanonicalText.find(
+            marker, markerPosition + 1U);
+    }
+    return false;
+}

+bool ReviewIdentityMatchesPayload(
+    int reviewContractVersion,
+    const std::string& reviewCanonicalText,
+    const std::string& reviewIdentityHash,
+    long long followUpProposalId,
+    int proposalContractVersion,
+    const std::string& proposalCanonicalText,
+    const std::string& proposalIdentityHash,
+    RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalReviewDecision reviewDecision,
+    const std::string& reviewerIdentity)
+{
+    const std::string marker =
+        ";reviewer=" + LengthPrefixed(reviewerIdentity) + ";reason=";
+    std::size_t markerPosition = reviewCanonicalText.find(marker);
+    while (markerPosition != std::string::npos)
+    {
+        const std::size_t lengthPosition = markerPosition + marker.size();
+        const std::size_t colonPosition =
+            reviewCanonicalText.find(':', lengthPosition);
+        if (colonPosition != std::string::npos &&
+            colonPosition > lengthPosition)
+        {
+            std::size_t reasonLength = 0U;
+            bool validLength = true;
+            for (std::size_t index = lengthPosition;
+                 index < colonPosition; ++index)
+            {
+                const unsigned char character =
+                    static_cast<unsigned char>(reviewCanonicalText[index]);
+                if (character < '0' || character > '9')
+                {
+                    validLength = false;
+                    break;
+                }
+                const std::size_t digit = character - '0';
+                if (reasonLength >
+                    (std::numeric_limits<std::size_t>::max() - digit) / 10U)
+                {
+                    validLength = false;
+                    break;
+                }
+                reasonLength = reasonLength * 10U + digit;
+            }
+            const std::size_t reasonPosition = colonPosition + 1U;
+            if (validLength && reasonLength ==
+                    reviewCanonicalText.size() - reasonPosition)
+            {
+                try
+                {
+                    const auto review =
+                        BuildRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalReview(
+                            reviewContractVersion, followUpProposalId,
+                            proposalContractVersion, proposalCanonicalText,
+                            proposalIdentityHash, reviewDecision,
+                            reviewerIdentity,
+                            reviewCanonicalText.substr(reasonPosition));
+                    if (review.identity.canonicalText == reviewCanonicalText &&
+                        review.identity.hash == reviewIdentityHash)
+                        return true;
+                }
+                catch (const std::exception&)
+                {
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        markerPosition = reviewCanonicalText.find(
+            marker, markerPosition + 1U);
+    }
+    return false;
+}

+bool ReviewIdentityMatchesPayload(
+    int reviewContractVersion,
+    const std::string& reviewCanonicalText,
+    const std::string& reviewIdentityHash,
+    long long followUpProposalId,
+    int proposalContractVersion,
+    const std::string& proposalCanonicalText,
+    const std::string& proposalIdentityHash,
+    RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalReviewDecision reviewDecision,
+    const std::string& reviewerIdentity)
+{
+    const std::string marker =
+        ";reviewer=" + LengthPrefixed(reviewerIdentity) + ";reason=";
+    std::size_t markerPosition = reviewCanonicalText.find(marker);
+    while (markerPosition != std::string::npos)
+    {
+        const std::size_t lengthPosition = markerPosition + marker.size();
+        const std::size_t colonPosition =
+            reviewCanonicalText.find(':', lengthPosition);
+        if (colonPosition != std::string::npos &&
+            colonPosition > lengthPosition)
+        {
+            std::size_t reasonLength = 0U;
+            bool validLength = true;
+            for (std::size_t index = lengthPosition;
+                 index < colonPosition; ++index)
+            {
+                const unsigned char character =
+                    static_cast<unsigned char>(reviewCanonicalText[index]);
+                if (character < '0' || character > '9')
+                {
+                    validLength = false;
+                    break;
+                }
+                const std::size_t digit = character - '0';
+                if (reasonLength >
+                    (std::numeric_limits<std::size_t>::max() - digit) / 10U)
+                {
+                    validLength = false;
+                    break;
+                }
+                reasonLength = reasonLength * 10U + digit;
+            }
+            const std::size_t reasonPosition = colonPosition + 1U;
+            if (validLength && reasonLength ==
+                    reviewCanonicalText.size() - reasonPosition)
+            {
+                try
+                {
+                    const auto review =
+                        BuildRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalReview(
+                            reviewContractVersion, followUpProposalId,
+                            proposalContractVersion, proposalCanonicalText,
+                            proposalIdentityHash, reviewDecision,
+                            reviewerIdentity,
+                            reviewCanonicalText.substr(reasonPosition));
+                    if (review.identity.canonicalText == reviewCanonicalText &&
+                        review.identity.hash == reviewIdentityHash)
+                        return true;
+                }
+                catch (const std::exception&)
+                {
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        markerPosition = reviewCanonicalText.find(
+            marker, markerPosition + 1U);
+    }
+    return false;
+}

+bool ReviewIdentityMatchesPayload(
+    int reviewContractVersion,
+    const std::string& reviewCanonicalText,
+    const std::string& reviewIdentityHash,
+    long long followUpProposalId,
+    int proposalContractVersion,
+    const std::string& proposalCanonicalText,
+    const std::string& proposalIdentityHash,
+    RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalReviewDecision reviewDecision,
+    const std::string& reviewerIdentity)
+{
+    const std::string marker =
+        ";reviewer=" + LengthPrefixed(reviewerIdentity) + ";reason=";
+    std::size_t markerPosition = reviewCanonicalText.find(marker);
+    while (markerPosition != std::string::npos)
+    {
+        const std::size_t lengthPosition = markerPosition + marker.size();
+        const std::size_t colonPosition =
+            reviewCanonicalText.find(':', lengthPosition);
+        if (colonPosition != std::string::npos &&
+            colonPosition > lengthPosition)
+        {
+            std::size_t reasonLength = 0U;
+            bool validLength = true;
+            for (std::size_t index = lengthPosition;
+                 index < colonPosition; ++index)
+            {
+                const unsigned char character =
+                    static_cast<unsigned char>(reviewCanonicalText[index]);
+                if (character < '0' || character > '9')
+                {
+                    validLength = false;
+                    break;
+                }
+                const std::size_t digit = character - '0';
+                if (reasonLength >
+                    (std::numeric_limits<std::size_t>::max() - digit) / 10U)
+                {
+                    validLength = false;
+                    break;
+                }
+                reasonLength = reasonLength * 10U + digit;
+            }
+            const std::size_t reasonPosition = colonPosition + 1U;
+            if (validLength && reasonLength ==
+                    reviewCanonicalText.size() - reasonPosition)
+            {
+                try
+                {
+                    const auto review =
+                        BuildRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalReview(
+                            reviewContractVersion, followUpProposalId,
+                            proposalContractVersion, proposalCanonicalText,
+                            proposalIdentityHash, reviewDecision,
+                            reviewerIdentity,
+                            reviewCanonicalText.substr(reasonPosition));
+                    if (review.identity.canonicalText == reviewCanonicalText &&
+                        review.identity.hash == reviewIdentityHash)
+                        return true;
+                }
+                catch (const std::exception&)
+                {
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        markerPosition = reviewCanonicalText.find(
+            marker, markerPosition + 1U);
+    }
+    return false;
+}

+bool ReviewIdentityMatchesPayload(
+    int reviewContractVersion,
+    const std::string& reviewCanonicalText,
+    const std::string& reviewIdentityHash,
+    long long followUpProposalId,
+    int proposalContractVersion,
+    const std::string& proposalCanonicalText,
+    const std::string& proposalIdentityHash,
+    RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalReviewDecision reviewDecision,
+    const std::string& reviewerIdentity)
+{
+    const std::string marker =
+        ";reviewer=" + LengthPrefixed(reviewerIdentity) + ";reason=";
+    std::size_t markerPosition = reviewCanonicalText.find(marker);
+    while (markerPosition != std::string::npos)
+    {
+        const std::size_t lengthPosition = markerPosition + marker.size();
+        const std::size_t colonPosition =
+            reviewCanonicalText.find(':', lengthPosition);
+        if (colonPosition != std::string::npos &&
+            colonPosition > lengthPosition)
+        {
+            std::size_t reasonLength = 0U;
+            bool validLength = true;
+            for (std::size_t index = lengthPosition;
+                 index < colonPosition; ++index)
+            {
+                const unsigned char character =
+                    static_cast<unsigned char>(reviewCanonicalText[index]);
+                if (character < '0' || character > '9')
+                {
+                    validLength = false;
+                    break;
+                }
+                const std::size_t digit = character - '0';
+                if (reasonLength >
+                    (std::numeric_limits<std::size_t>::max() - digit) / 10U)
+                {
+                    validLength = false;
+                    break;
+                }
+                reasonLength = reasonLength * 10U + digit;
+            }
+            const std::size_t reasonPosition = colonPosition + 1U;
+            if (validLength && reasonLength ==
+                    reviewCanonicalText.size() - reasonPosition)
+            {
+                try
+                {
+                    const auto review =
+                        BuildRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalReview(
+                            reviewContractVersion, followUpProposalId,
+                            proposalContractVersion, proposalCanonicalText,
+                            proposalIdentityHash, reviewDecision,
+                            reviewerIdentity,
+                            reviewCanonicalText.substr(reasonPosition));
+                    if (review.identity.canonicalText == reviewCanonicalText &&
+                        review.identity.hash == reviewIdentityHash)
+                        return true;
+                }
+                catch (const std::exception&)
+                {
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        markerPosition = reviewCanonicalText.find(
+            marker, markerPosition + 1U);
+    }
+    return false;
+}

+bool ReviewIdentityMatchesPayload(
+    int reviewContractVersion,
+    const std::string& reviewCanonicalText,
+    const std::string& reviewIdentityHash,
+    long long followUpProposalId,
+    int proposalContractVersion,
+    const std::string& proposalCanonicalText,
+    const std::string& proposalIdentityHash,
+    RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalReviewDecision reviewDecision,
+    const std::string& reviewerIdentity)
+{
+    const std::string marker =
+        ";reviewer=" + LengthPrefixed(reviewerIdentity) + ";reason=";
+    std::size_t markerPosition = reviewCanonicalText.find(marker);
+    while (markerPosition != std::string::npos)
+    {
+        const std::size_t lengthPosition = markerPosition + marker.size();
+        const std::size_t colonPosition =
+            reviewCanonicalText.find(':', lengthPosition);
+        if (colonPosition != std::string::npos &&
+            colonPosition > lengthPosition)
+        {
+            std::size_t reasonLength = 0U;
+            bool validLength = true;
+            for (std::size_t index = lengthPosition;
+                 index < colonPosition; ++index)
+            {
+                const unsigned char character =
+                    static_cast<unsigned char>(reviewCanonicalText[index]);
+                if (character < '0' || character > '9')
+                {
+                    validLength = false;
+                    break;
+                }
+                const std::size_t digit = character - '0';
+                if (reasonLength >
+                    (std::numeric_limits<std::size_t>::max() - digit) / 10U)
+                {
+                    validLength = false;
+                    break;
+                }
+                reasonLength = reasonLength * 10U + digit;
+            }
+            const std::size_t reasonPosition = colonPosition + 1U;
+            if (validLength && reasonLength ==
+                    reviewCanonicalText.size() - reasonPosition)
+            {
+                try
+                {
+                    const auto review =
+                        BuildRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalReview(
+                            reviewContractVersion, followUpProposalId,
+                            proposalContractVersion, proposalCanonicalText,
+                            proposalIdentityHash, reviewDecision,
+                            reviewerIdentity,
+                            reviewCanonicalText.substr(reasonPosition));
+                    if (review.identity.canonicalText == reviewCanonicalText &&
+                        review.identity.hash == reviewIdentityHash)
+                        return true;
+                }
+                catch (const std::exception&)
+                {
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        markerPosition = reviewCanonicalText.find(
+            marker, markerPosition + 1U);
+    }
+    return false;
+}

+bool ReviewIdentityMatchesPayload(
+    int reviewContractVersion,
+    const std::string& reviewCanonicalText,
+    const std::string& reviewIdentityHash,
+    long long followUpProposalId,
+    int proposalContractVersion,
+    const std::string& proposalCanonicalText,
+    const std::string& proposalIdentityHash,
+    RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalReviewDecision reviewDecision,
+    const std::string& reviewerIdentity)
+{
+    const std::string marker =
+        ";reviewer=" + LengthPrefixed(reviewerIdentity) + ";reason=";
+    std::size_t markerPosition = reviewCanonicalText.find(marker);
+    while (markerPosition != std::string::npos)
+    {
+        const std::size_t lengthPosition = markerPosition + marker.size();
+        const std::size_t colonPosition =
+            reviewCanonicalText.find(':', lengthPosition);
+        if (colonPosition != std::string::npos &&
+            colonPosition > lengthPosition)
+        {
+            std::size_t reasonLength = 0U;
+            bool validLength = true;
+            for (std::size_t index = lengthPosition;
+                 index < colonPosition; ++index)
+            {
+                const unsigned char character =
+                    static_cast<unsigned char>(reviewCanonicalText[index]);
+                if (character < '0' || character > '9')
+                {
+                    validLength = false;
+                    break;
+                }
+                const std::size_t digit = character - '0';
+                if (reasonLength >
+                    (std::numeric_limits<std::size_t>::max() - digit) / 10U)
+                {
+                    validLength = false;
+                    break;
+                }
+                reasonLength = reasonLength * 10U + digit;
+            }
+            const std::size_t reasonPosition = colonPosition + 1U;
+            if (validLength && reasonLength ==
+                    reviewCanonicalText.size() - reasonPosition)
+            {
+                try
+                {
+                    const auto review =
+                        BuildRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalReview(
+                            reviewContractVersion, followUpProposalId,
+                            proposalContractVersion, proposalCanonicalText,
+                            proposalIdentityHash, reviewDecision,
+                            reviewerIdentity,
+                            reviewCanonicalText.substr(reasonPosition));
+                    if (review.identity.canonicalText == reviewCanonicalText &&
+                        review.identity.hash == reviewIdentityHash)
+                        return true;
+                }
+                catch (const std::exception&)
+                {
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        markerPosition = reviewCanonicalText.find(
+            marker, markerPosition + 1U);
+    }
+    return false;
+}

     if (value.empty() ||

+bool ReviewIdentityMatchesPayload(
+    int reviewContractVersion,
+    const std::string& reviewCanonicalText,
+    const std::string& reviewIdentityHash,
+    long long followUpProposalId,
+    int proposalContractVersion,
+    const std::string& proposalCanonicalText,
+    const std::string& proposalIdentityHash,
+    RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalReviewDecision reviewDecision,
+    const std::string& reviewerIdentity)
+{
+    const std::string marker =
+        ";reviewer=" + LengthPrefixed(reviewerIdentity) + ";reason=";
+    std::size_t markerPosition = reviewCanonicalText.find(marker);
+    while (markerPosition != std::string::npos)
+    {
+        const std::size_t lengthPosition = markerPosition + marker.size();
+        const std::size_t colonPosition =
+            reviewCanonicalText.find(':', lengthPosition);
+        if (colonPosition != std::string::npos &&
+            colonPosition > lengthPosition)
+        {
+            std::size_t reasonLength = 0U;
+            bool validLength = true;
+            for (std::size_t index = lengthPosition;
+                 index < colonPosition; ++index)
+            {
+                const unsigned char character =
+                    static_cast<unsigned char>(reviewCanonicalText[index]);
+                if (character < '0' || character > '9')
+                {
+                    validLength = false;
+                    break;
+                }
+                const std::size_t digit = character - '0';
+                if (reasonLength >
+                    (std::numeric_limits<std::size_t>::max() - digit) / 10U)
+                {
+                    validLength = false;
+                    break;
+                }
+                reasonLength = reasonLength * 10U + digit;
+            }
+            const std::size_t reasonPosition = colonPosition + 1U;
+            if (validLength && reasonLength ==
+                    reviewCanonicalText.size() - reasonPosition)
+            {
+                try
+                {
+                    const auto review =
+                        BuildRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalReview(
+                            reviewContractVersion, followUpProposalId,
+                            proposalContractVersion, proposalCanonicalText,
+                            proposalIdentityHash, reviewDecision,
+                            reviewerIdentity,
+                            reviewCanonicalText.substr(reasonPosition));
+                    if (review.identity.canonicalText == reviewCanonicalText &&
+                        review.identity.hash == reviewIdentityHash)
+                        return true;
+                }
+                catch (const std::exception&)
+                {
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        markerPosition = reviewCanonicalText.find(
+            marker, markerPosition + 1U);
+    }
+    return false;
+}
